alignments.note: The adverb is rendered by a prepositional phrase; the supplied preposition and determiner are rule 7 helpers, headed on the nominal word.

ἔννυχα (*by night*) is rendered *before day*, headed on the nominal word. The division of *a great while before day* between this token and λίαν is a judgment call: giving *before day* to the night word and *a great while* to the intensifier keeps each token's own sense recoverable.
λίαν (*exceedingly*) is rendered by the degree phrase *a great while*, headed on the nominal word. See the note on ἔννυχα for the competing division.
Rule 106: *up* realizes the preverb ἀνα-; the supplied subject is a rule 9 helper, headed on the verb word.
Rule 88: the supplied juncture *and* is a helper on the finite verb it introduces; *out* realizes the preverb ἐξ- under rule 106.
Finite verb; the preverb ἀπ- has no separate English word.
Rule 58: adjective and noun both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Rule 55: a crasis token takes both English words as one unit, headed on the pronominal element.

review_notes: The division of *a great while before day* between ἔννυχα and λίαν is the verse's main open judgment; both units carry the reasoning.
